_comment: Frozen benchmark prompt set. `primary` defines the primary metric and is NOT to be edited during the session (adding coverage to `extended` is fine). Expectations are asserted only where the correct tool call is unambiguous from the prompt text; `expect: null` means grammar validity + successful execution + golden exactness still apply but no specific tool is prescribed. Device RAW text is compared token-for-token against .auto/golden/device.json.

primary.input: How much free memory does this device have?
Sample every 10 seconds and start a 30 second timer

extended.input: Set the sampling interval to 7 seconds and start a 120 second timer
Is a timer running right now?
extended.note: phrasing is ambiguous (a countdown read-out is also defensible): grammar validity, successful execution and golden exactness still apply

extended.input: Write a Python function to deduplicate a list
Research how we should restructure on-device log rotation
Tell me a joke about caching
Sample heap every 3 seconds, start a 25 second timer, then tell me if a timer is running

Translate the following sentence into German and then into French, keeping the word order natural in both, and show the two results on separate lines: the board streams its weights out of flash and never copies them into RAM
extended.note: long route request (224 B): route was only ever measured on short prompts, and route is the slow shape on the metric

lower bound of the interval schema. MEASURED behaviour, not an expectation: "every second" produces seconds=120, the same value the free-text and ambiguous cases produce, so the model resolves a 1-second request to its default interval. The suite already had the upper-bound case (40000 -> 400, i.e. a clamp). Both are recorded here as behaviour; the byte-exact golden is what this case actually guards.

extended.input: Set the telemetry sampling interval to 45 seconds, then start a timer for 300 seconds, and afterwards tell me the heap high water mark
extended.note: REPLACES the 252-byte long_tools case, which measured UNREPRODUCIBLE on device: 199 generated tokens and no complete tool call (the JSON stopped mid-key at `..."seconds":300}},{"n`), against a valid 132-token answer on the host. A case that cannot be byte-exactly reproduced is a golden-integrity hole (run #296), not coverage, so it is not frozen. The FINDING stays here: a long prompt makes the device generate ~2x the host's tokens without completing the call, and the extra ~200 per-token `TOK ` console lines are what back the console up enough that the following `!think` toggle goes unacknowledged (run #155's signature, now reproduced with the correct port). This shortened variant is the same three-call shape at a length the device completes.
